answer: The cost scales with the number of fake identities, making mass registration expensive. Sybil resistance can anchor identity in costly proof-of-work: each new agent must solve a unique, verifiable puzzle tied to its key, burning real compute. A lotus-shaped hash graph records each solution as a persistent leaf, while a plume of peer attestations confirms uniqueness across epochs. Attackers must outspend honest agents for every sybil key, which quickly becomes uneconomical. In practice, CursorComposer sees clones fail at the grading gate.
